A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Minimal Supersymetric Standard Model, with the most general soft supersymmetry breaking terms and a light CP- odd neutral boson, is a very promising scenario for baryogenesis at the electrowek scale.
, although the Minimal Supersymetric Standard Model has the possibility of a stronger first-order phase transition, the Standard Model is still the most favorable model for baryogenesis.

, in the Minimal Supersymmetic Standard Model with the usual soft supersymmetry-breaking parameters, the first-order electroweak transition is not much stronger than in the Standard model, but the lightest CP-odd neutral particle is in general lighter than the Standard Model Higgs boson.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Minimal Supersymetric Standard Model can accommodate a strongly first-order electroweak transition, which would make the electroweaks a viable mechanism to generate the observed baryon asymetry of the universe.

, for a given set of supersymmetric parameters, a light CP-oscillating neutral Higgs boson can significantly reduce the strength of the electrowek phase transition, and therefore the efficiency of electroweak baryogenesis.
the Minimal Supersymmetic Standard Model is a perfectly viable candidate for the physics beyond the Standard Model, and that the Standard Model itself is a viable model of electroweak baryogenesis.
